newsitem.title: USA: NYC Council wants to curb tobacco ads near schools.
newsitem.headline: NYC Council wants to curb tobacco ads near schools.

text.p: The New York City Council, one of the first to restrict smoking in restaurants and workplaces, plans to unveil a bill on Wednesday that would curb tobacco advertising near schools.
The measure would restrict advertising and promotion of tobacco products within 1,000 feet of schools and other places where children gather, the council said in a statement.

"This is a logical extension of the council's campaign to use the power of law to educate people about the dangers of smoking," City Council Speaker Peter Vallone said in a statement released on Tuesday by his spokeswoman.
"We have to get children to understand what we didn't know or understand when we were their age," said Vallone, who will formally announce the bill at a news conference on Wednesday.

Mary Carnovale, a spokeswoman for Philip Morris Cos Inc, said the New York-based maker of Marlboro and other cigarettes had not been given a chance to review the bill, but she said its initial reaction was not favorable.
"It appears the proposal goes far beyond the issue of youth access to severely restricting the rights of manufacturers and storeowners to truthfully advertize a legal product," she said.

She declined to say whether the company would fight the proposed restrictions, saying only: "Phillip Morris believes the key to reducing youth smoking lies in restricting access, not commercial free speech."
Since April 1995, New York City has sharply limited smoking in restaurants, workplaces and other public areas.

The speaker, a Democrat running for re-election, is seen as potential candidate in next year's gubernatorial race. The new bill would have to be approved by Republican Mayor Rudolph Giuliani. The mayor's spokeswoman had no immediate comment.
The Supreme Court has declined to hear a challenge to a Baltimore law that banned cigarette and liquor ads on many billboards.
